subject: Priv infra: module ownership & CI gating for on-prem/VPC bundles
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie@acmecloud.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmecloud.io
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment - initial IaC bundle and ownership ask

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion, I'm attaching the initial tarball of our on-prem orchestration modules (Terraform + Helm + Ansible stubs). We need Redwood to confirm recommended ownership boundaries and CI gating expectations before we hand the repo over to the integrators.

Highlights:
- Terraform modules for VPC, subnets, and peering (modules/vpc/*)
- Helm charts for runtime (charts/redwood-runtime/*)
- Ansible playbooks for node prep (ansible/provision/*)

Primary asks:
1) Can you map which Redwood module should be maintained by Customer Ops vs Redwood infra (network vs runtime)?
2) What tests/CI gates do you require for private deployments (Terraform plan checks, Helm chart lint + integration, Ansible idempotency)
3) Any network policy guardrails you'd insist on (eg. deny-by-default egress, control plane ports)?

I attached priv-modules-v2.tgz and a short network-policy-review.md. Jamie

[Attachment: priv-modules-v2.tgz (2.3MB)]
[Attachment: network-policy-review.md (8KB)]

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: jamie@acmecloud.io
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - initial IaC bundle and ownership ask

Team — forwarding the Acme bundle. High level: Acme wants clear ownership split and a CI gating checklist before engineering handoff. I'd like a short internal review and proposed ownership matrix by EOD Friday so we can give them a crisp answer.

Key items to cover:
- Module ownership (who supports VPC vs runtime vs ops automation)
- Minimal CI gates for Redwood-managed modules (tf fmt/validate/plan, helm lint + smoke deploy, ansible-lint + dry-run)
- Network policy defaults and required exceptions for control plane and telemetry
- Release cadence and pinning strategy (semantic tags, image digest locking)

Ben/Evelyn: please coordinate on Terraform/Helm boundaries. Mina: focus on Ansible idempotency and onboarding docs. I'll own the ownership matrix and customer communication.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: jamie@acmecloud.io
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - initial IaC bundle and ownership ask

Markus — quick read through attached tarball. A few immediate notes:

- Terraform: the vpc module is pretty standard, but they mix control-plane peering with customer network definitions in a single module. We should ask them to split "control-plane-network" vs "tenant-network" so we can take ownership of control-plane peering and routing.
- Helm: charts need imagePullPolicy and digest pinning; several values.yaml entries rely on latest tags. We'll require a chart pre-release job that verifies digest locking.
- CI: propose mandatory checks for Redwood-managed modules: terraform fmt/validate/plan with a backend state check; helm lint + helm test (smoke); and a terraform-cost-estimate check.

Attaching a small patch with CI pipeline changes (ci-pipeline-diff.patch) that shows required steps — it's opinionated but minimal.

I can draft the ownership matrix with suggested SLAs.

-Ben
[Attachment: ci-pipeline-diff.patch]

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: jamie@acmecloud.io
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - initial IaC bundle and ownership ask

Adding a few network-focused items inline — copied from network-policy-review.md: 

> Recommended defaults:
> - Deny all ingress to runtime nodes except control-plane ports (TCP 443, 8443) and telemetry endpoints.
> - Egress: allow kubelet/registry outbound; otherwise deny-by-default with explicit exceptions.
> - Peering must be routable only through explicit route tables; no broad 0.0.0.0/0 routes on peered subnets.

We should require a network-policy acceptance test in CI that deploys a small pod and validates that cross-namespace policies block unwanted flows. If Acme can't run that in their CI, Redwood can offer a temporary sandbox job during onboarding.

Evelyn
Senior Network Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: jamie@acmecloud.io
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - initial IaC bundle and ownership ask

Reviewed the Ansible playbooks. A couple of practical asks:

- Replace raw shell tasks with modules (user, package, systemd) so idempotency is testable.
- Add a molecule test that validates node prep (accounts, kernel params, docker/containerd config).
- Document supported OS images and kernel thresholds in the README (we should block unsupported kernels in an early preflight).

I'll prepare a short checklist and a sample molecule job we can offer Acme as a CI snippet.

-Mina
Infrastructure Automation Lead

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: jamie@acmecloud.io
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - initial IaC bundle and ownership ask

Jamie — thanks for the bundle and patience while we reviewed. Summary of what Redwood proposes (short deliverable list):

1) Ownership matrix (attached) — Redwood will own control-plane networking modules, runtime Helm charts (security/hardening), and the release gating for any Redwood-managed modules. Acme retains tenant-network and tenant-facing infra.
2) CI gating: mandatory pipeline steps for Redwood-managed modules: terraform fmt/validate/plan + state-check, helm lint + digest pin check + smoke deploy, ansible-lint + molecule node-prep smoke test. We'll share CI snippets for GitHub Actions/GitLab.
3) Network guardrails: deny-by-default egress/ingress, explicit route tables for peering, telemetry ports allowed. Optional: Redwood sandbox job to validate network policies during onboarding.
4) Release strategy: semantic tags + immutable image digests; Redwood will maintain a minor-compatible backport branch for patches for the first 90 days post-release.

Attachments: a compact ownership matrix CSV and the CI patch Ben proposed. If that sounds good, we'll send a short MOU paragraph (non-binding) and then open a repo with split modules for our teams to iterate.

Best,
Markus
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ownership-matrix.csv (3KB)]
